conventions.convention: The reference measure is arbitrary; target and proposal shapes have strictly positive finite normalizers, and the finite positive envelope constant dominates the target shape almost everywhere.

Inputs are ideal independent proposal draws with normalized law G and independent uniform draws on (0,1); the proposal-uniform pairs are mutually IID. The acceptance function is zero at zero proposal density and otherwise is the density ratio clipped at one.

Extended-valued shapes in the acceptance theorem are replaced by finite measurable representatives on a common measurable null exception; this leaves both density measures and the output law unchanged.
N counts proposals through and including the first accepted proposal, so its geometric distribution starts at one. The geometric-series convention includes q^0=1 when q=0.
The counting-measure theorem uses N={0,1,2,...}, the full power-set sigma-algebra, and the nonnegative extended series starting at zero, including infinite sums.

load_bearing.statement: For i=1,2,..., draw (Y_i,U_i). If U_i ≤ a(Y_i), return Y_i and stop; otherwise continue to the next pair. Here a(y)=0 when the proposal shape is zero and otherwise is min{1, target shape/(c times proposal shape)}.

For measurable nonnegative shapes on an arbitrary measure space with 0<Z_f,Z_g<∞ and a finite c>0 satisfying target shape ≤ c times proposal shape almost everywhere, rejection sampling with proposal law G terminates almost surely, has per-proposal acceptance probability p=Z_f/(cZ_g), and returns a law assigning every measurable A the mass (1/Z_f) times the integral of the target shape over A.
In the acceptance-law theorem's setup, with p=Z_f/(cZ_g) and q=1-p, P(N=k)=q^(k-1)p for every integer k≥1 and E[N]=1/p=cZ_g/Z_f. For normalized target and proposal densities, E[N]=c.
For every measurable f:N→[0,+∞], where N={0,1,2,...} has counting measure on its power set, the integral of f equals the nonnegative extended series sum from n=0 to infinity of f(n).
